decision: Use as historical community fishery-context evidence and a discovery lead only. Do not treat questionnaire responses or the paper's aggregate resource counts as a specimen-based species inventory, verified occurrence dataset, catch estimate, or current status.

source.title: Socio-ecological system assessment for conservation planning in riverine and mangrove fishery areas in Bataan, Philippines
source.citation: Corpuz, M. N. C., & Espaldon, M. V. O. (2023). AACL Bioflux, 16(2), 1114-1126.
source.access: Publisher PDF text was accessible for review; no local raw copy was retained.
source.itemSpecificReuseTerms: Not confirmed in this review. No article figures, photographs, or extended prose are reproduced.

studyScope.mapAndGeometry: Figure 1 labels the four broad riverine fishery areas. The Bataan coordinate in the introduction is contextual and is not identified as a sampling station. No study-area boundary geometry or per-interview coordinates are supplied.
studyScope.samplingMethod: Questionnaire-based socio-ecological assessment using interviews in four coastal villages; the paper reports 192 respondents. It also describes local mediators, interviews with local fisheries specialists, and some focus groups.
studyScope.exactInterviewDates: No exact interview dates were identified in the reviewed study-protocol passages.
studyScope.biologicalSampling: The reported method is interviews/questionnaires, not a fish-capture survey with identified specimens, vouchers, or station-level biological samples.

reportedFisheryInformation.aggregateClaimAsPublished: The abstract reports no less than 30 fish species among the riverine and mangrove fishery resources indicated by local respondents, alongside crustacean and mollusk resource groups.
reportedFisheryInformation.aggregateCountMeaning: Community-reported resource summary; not an independently verified species-richness count or a complete taxonomic list.

examplesAsReported.label: Sarotherodon melanotheron
examplesAsReported.context: Identified in the paper as black-chin tilapia and discussed as an introduced fishery resource.

examplesAsReported.label: Oreochromis niloticus
examplesAsReported.context: Identified in the paper as Nile tilapia and discussed as an introduced fishery resource.

examplesAsReported.label: Liza sp.
examplesAsReported.context: Mullets are discussed as a fishery resource, including a genus-level label.

examplesAsReported.label: Glossogobius spp., Rhinogobius spp., and Neogobius spp.
examplesAsReported.context: The paper says its 'gobies' category aggregates diminutive fishery resources from multiple genera; not a species-level identification.

examplesAsReported.label: Anguilla sp.
examplesAsReported.context: The text treats eel as a resource; a later parenthetical says it is most probably Anguilla marmorata, which remains an attributed uncertainty rather than a confirmed identification.

reportedFisheryInformation.retrospectiveChangeClaim: Reported declines over the last 40 years are respondents' recalled perceptions, not a standardized time series or measured population trend.

relationshipToOtherBataanEvidence.2025ThreeRiverSurvey: The 2023 and 2025 papers share authors and discuss Almacen, Bagac, and Talisay. The 2023 paper is interview-based and covers Morong as well; overlap of respondents, field periods, or underlying data has not been established. Do not count it as independent biological corroboration for the 2025 survey.

nextStep: If these reports are needed for a future community-knowledge feature, seek the questionnaire/codebook, interview date range, site-level response definitions, and reuse conditions. Keep that feature separate from verified biological occurrence and current catchability.
